The Beijing example contains one simulation day on a directed road network:
11,742 displayed edges and 288 five-minute intervals from 00:00 to 24:00.
The map has relative-load, interval-change and high-load-duration views.
The initial interval is 08:50 to 08:55.

## Map and data

The map supports pan, zoom, playback and interval selection. A road popup
shows its edge ID, endpoints, road type, length and value for the selected
interval. The frame summary reports active edges, high-load edges and load
statistics. The highest-value edges appear beside the map.

The HTML embeds the traffic data, offline OSM geometry and Leaflet 1.9.4.
The documentation panel contains the field definitions, preparation method,
reference figures and statistics. The figures and tables below describe
08:50 to 08:55; the map readouts follow the selected interval.

## Source and data preparation

The project document `个体轨迹数据拥堵溯源分析项目及数据说明.docx` identifies
`output_agent.csv` and `output_LinkTDMOE.csv` as simulation outputs, with
`input_node.csv` and `input_link.csv` defining the network. This example uses
the road-level export `saturation_dynamic_leaflet_osm_osmgeom.html`, identified
by filename and checksum in the data provenance.

Snapshot preparation extracts nine JSON assignments from that export and
serializes them into `data/beijing-visualization.json.gz`. The assignments
supply road geometry, sparse relative loads, duration records, interval
summaries and display metadata. Numeric values use the precision in the
export. The preparation code takes a source export as its input:

```{r preparation, eval=FALSE}
source_html <- 'saturation_dynamic_leaflet_osm_osmgeom.html'
source_lines <- readLines(source_html, warn=FALSE, encoding='UTF-8')
keys <- c('network','flowByBin','durationByBin','timeMeta','timeBins',
          'bounds','congestionStops','timeBinMinutes','metricKey')
literal <- function(key) {
  pattern <- paste0('^\\s*const ', key, '\\s*=\\s*')
  candidates <- sub(';\\s*$', '', sub(pattern, '',
                    grep(pattern, source_lines, value=TRUE)))
  candidates <- candidates[vapply(candidates, jsonlite::validate, logical(1))]
  stopifnot(length(candidates)==1L)
  candidates
}
payload <- paste(paste0('"',keys,'":',vapply(keys,literal,'')),collapse=',')
provenance <- jsonlite::toJSON(list(source_html=basename(source_html),
  source_md5=unname(tools::md5sum(source_html))),auto_unbox=TRUE)
artifact <- paste0('{"schema_version":1,"source":"beijing","provenance":',
                   provenance,',"payload":{',payload,'}}')
output_file <- 'data/beijing-visualization.json.gz'
stopifnot(!file.exists(output_file))
dir.create(dirname(output_file), recursive=TRUE, showWarnings=FALSE)
con <- gzfile(output_file, 'wt')
tryCatch(writeLines(artifact, con, useBytes=TRUE), finally=close(con))
```

The HTML build reads the packaged snapshot and `data/osm-basemap.json.gz`.
`map-template.html` defines the map interface and includes Leaflet's script,
styles and license. `run.R` renders this R Markdown document in a temporary
directory and embeds it with both datasets in `beijing-traffic-maps.html`.

## Fields and coverage

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace('bdynets', quietly=TRUE)) {
  package_file <- 'bdynets_0.1.0.tar.gz'
  if (!file.exists(package_file)) stop('Bundled bdynets source package is absent')
  package_library <- tempfile('traffic-r-library-')
  dir.create(package_library)
  .libPaths(c(package_library, .libPaths()))
  install.packages(package_file, repos=NULL, type='source',
                   lib=package_library, quiet=TRUE)
  if (!requireNamespace('bdynets', quietly=TRUE))
    stop('Bundled bdynets package installation failed')
}
library(bdynets)
source('osm-figures.R')
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path=file.path(tempdir(),'beijing-figure-'),message=FALSE)
```

```{r data}
snapshot <- read_traffic_data(params$snapshot)
stopifnot(snapshot$source=='beijing', length(snapshot$bins)==288L,
          snapshot$bin_minutes==5L,
          snapshot$time_meta[[as.character(snapshot$bins[1])]]$start_min==0,
          snapshot$time_meta[[as.character(tail(snapshot$bins,1))]]$end_min==1440)
knitr::kable(data.frame(edges=length(snapshot$ids), frames=length(snapshot$bins),
                       minutes_per_frame=snapshot$bin_minutes))
```

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| `schema_version`, `source`, `provenance` | Wrapper format, dataset identifier and source filename/checksums. |
| `network` | GeoJSON lines in longitude/latitude order. Edge attributes include index, ID, from/to node IDs, length in km, lanes, speed limit and road type. |
| `flowByBin` | Sparse `[edge_index, relative_load]` pairs for each interval. Relative load is `x_ijt / estimated capacity`, rounded to three decimals. |
| `durationByBin` | Sparse edge records giving consecutive high-load duration in five-minute bins. |
| `timeBins`, `timeMeta` | Interval order, minute boundaries and frame summaries. |
| `bounds` | Southwest and northeast corners in latitude/longitude order. |
| `congestionStops` | Color thresholds at 0%, 20%, 40%, 60% and 80% load. |
| `timeBinMinutes`, `metricKey` | Interval width of five minutes and the metric identifier `saturation`. |

An edge absent from a sparse interval has zero displayed load. The denominator
in the load ratio is an empirical count estimate. The ratio measures simulated
occupancy relative to that estimate; it does not measure speed or congestion
probability.

## Relative load, change and duration

```{r figures, fig.width=9, fig.height=7, out.width='100%'}
frames <- traffic_osm_figures(params$snapshot, 'beijing',
                          time_index=params$time_index)
```

The load view uses five color classes. Gray traffic edges have zero displayed
load. In the change view, red shows an increase from the preceding interval
and blue a decrease; line width scales with the size of the change. The first
interval has no preceding observation. The duration view expresses consecutive
high-load bins in minutes.

High load is defined by the source's 80% threshold before display rounding.
A displayed value of 0.800 can therefore differ from a threshold test on the
rounded array. Duration comes from `durationByBin`. Traffic lines use their
stored polylines and Web Mercator projection. Reference-figure widths are
scaled for static display; the interactive view uses browser pixel widths.

## Selected-frame statistics

```{r summary}
statistics <- unlist(frames$current$summary)
knitr::kable(data.frame(statistic=names(statistics), value=unname(statistics)))
```

`active_edges` counts positive displayed loads. `congested_edges` is the
high-load count from the frame record. The share fields divide these counts
by all 11,742 displayed edges. `mean_metric`, `p95_metric` and `max_metric`
describe the frame's active-edge load distribution. At 08:50 to 08:55, the
mean is `r frames$current$summary$mean_metric` and the high-load count is
`r frames$current$summary$congested_edges`.

`total_xijt` is a sum of edge-interval occupancy counts. A vehicle can
contribute to several edges or intervals, so this sum is not a count of
unique vehicles.

## Offline basemap

`data/osm-basemap.json.gz` contains generalized roads, water polygons and place
labels from the Protomaps OSM archive dated 20 October 2026. The extract uses
zoom 11 and the traffic extent plus a 0.02-degree margin. `download_osm.py`
contains the extraction procedure. Cache provenance includes the archive URL,
retrieval time, tile hashes and a geometry checksum.

OSM is geographic context. Traffic values and road connectivity come from
the traffic dataset. Place labels are spaced to reduce overlap. The basemap's
date describes the geographic extract, rather than the simulation date.

Map data: [OpenStreetMap contributors](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright),
via [Protomaps](https://docs.protomaps.com/basemaps/downloads), ODbL Produced Work.

## Build and figure export

`Rscript run.R` builds the HTML from this folder. R dependencies are `jsonlite`,
`rmarkdown`, `knitr`, `magrittr` and `bdynets`; HTML conversion uses Pandoc.
`bdynets_0.1.0.tar.gz` contains the version 0.1.0 source package and license.
The entrypoint uses that local archive in a temporary R library when the
package is absent. Viewing the HTML requires a current browser.

The R plotting index runs from 1 to 288. Index 107 is 08:50 to 08:55; index 97
is 08:00 to 08:05. A figure-export call has the following form:

```{r export-example, eval=FALSE}
traffic_osm_figures(params$snapshot, 'beijing', time_index=97L,
                output_dir='output/beijing-0800')
```

`osm-figures.R` provides PDF/PNG figure export and source records. Basemap
preparation uses Python packages `requests`, `pmtiles` and
`mapbox-vector-tile`. The HTML build and figure export use the packaged data
and cache.

## Interpretation

The example describes road-level simulated load. It contains display geometry,
frame values and aggregate statistics. Vehicle trajectories and raw occupancy
records are outside this snapshot. Rounded load ratios support descriptive
maps; congestion-source attribution requires a separate analysis of vehicle
movements and time alignment.
